questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to find a university that was ranking wise at least as good or better than KU. UofT was perfect as I had challenging graduate courses while also being able to travel a lot!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most things need to be figured out on your own, but it is definitely doable. Go to one of the introductions (there are only a few). But most can be found on their website if you click around.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Barely any. Most things you'll need to figure out on your own. There is a club fair in the start and some introductory events which are nice, but other than that not much.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There just isn't much in intro in grad school anywhere I think.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Pretty hard if a month or less till exchange, BEWARE: in toronto accomodation without windows do exists... and while amberstudent did provide housing you really need to be careful of what you agree to. (Most agreements are binding unless another person can take over your lease.)
Ended up in an Airbnb for 3 months with another exchange student. Not as expensive as one would expect and it was miles better than my first accommodation with amberstudent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Begin early, 3-4 months in advance makes your life much easier. While it is possible to find earlier, it is substantially cheaper 
(Tartu e.g. good location, cheap, but still has some minor issue)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I couldn't register courses via acorn, but I emailed someone (details in next box) and after that everything went pretty smooth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
I emailed an administrator from the department of statistical sciences (graduate). I had a zoom meeting with the administrator and a professor and got all the courses I wanted! 
NOTE: You cannot register on acorn (like you're supposed to) so contact someone depending on your area of study. Multiple people had this issue.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got every class I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Especially if you are a graduate student: Reach out to someone at your department to ensure they know what courses you want. 
Some people had trouble getting courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fun and challenging and there was help if you reached out. Can be tough if you take advanced classes, undergraduate is a lot easier (at least in statistics), but there can be a lot of work (Assingments).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took Advanced Time Series, Advanced Computational Statistics and Time Series. I really enjoyed the courses, however the two advanced courses were tough and we did not have many exercises to prepare for the exam. (and passing as a graduate student is 70% or above btw, they do curve the grade if the course is really hard in stats)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More applied. I was used to having lecture notes written by my professors, but there most classes are done with slides (A north American thing).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked all of my courses, but MCMC  (monte carlo markov chain)
which we had about in Advanced Computational Statistics.

questions.answer:
(btw I biked in toronto that's why transport was low)
Traveling costs are not included.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food. Most foods are simply more expensive in grocery stores. Eating out is cheaper in Toronto than in Copenhagen, but still expensive in the long run.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really like some of the clubs I joined! Vic Bachata and New resonance (an a capella club)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
3 free gyms at st. george campus, plenty of sports, really nice sports facilities.
(Plenty to do in toronto)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joining a club is fun. And join or create an instagram group with other exchange students. (We had a big one with 250 exchange students!)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Algonquin provincial park super nice in fall! probably also summer or spring. (Autumn colors are beautiful)

We had a reading week and vancouver/ whistler is super nice if you like nature and hiking!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, Toronto is super international friendly. A lot of people are international!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to clubs and engage whenever possible.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food. Finding a new rythm for that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The international environment. (not much canadian culture though)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find housing early
2. Find groups of exchange students (in big insta groups a lot of people suggest events or happenings in the start!) 
3.Travel

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open and try new stuff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other exchange students and traveling with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing, figuring out all information and food habits.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
